title: Work-graph abstraction integrity
description:
Close the semantic and boundary gaps found in the July 2026 work-graph architecture review: containment stability under transitive reduction, a single hierarchy-resolution implementation across all consumers, one blocking predicate, graph primitives owned by the graph layer, atomic template instantiation with config-declared role bindings, and unambiguous naming.

## Background

The review confirmed the core model is sound: one persisted edge primitive (`Issue.dependencies`), hierarchy derived from the DAG plus type levels, labels advisory, all edge writes funneled through one cycle-checked path. It also found structural weaknesses: transitive reduction deletes the direct edges the hierarchy resolver treats as containment signal; the web UI hand-maintains a TypeScript port of the resolver because no API serves resolution; the dependency-met rule is encoded four times with drift; command handlers hand-roll graph traversal; template apply is non-atomic and reaches for hardcoded role names; four module/CLI name collisions invite conflation.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: Resolved hierarchy (parent, children, cluster, rank) is invariant under addition or removal of transitively-redundant dependency edges.
- [hard] REQ-2: Exactly one implementation of hierarchy resolution exists in the repository, and every consumer (CLI, HTTP server, web UI) consumes its output.
- [hard] REQ-3: The dependency-met rule is defined once in the domain layer and reused by every surface that reports or enforces blocking.
- [hard] REQ-4: Graph traversal and acyclicity primitives live in the graph layer; command handlers contain no hand-rolled graph walks.
- [hard] REQ-5: Template application validates fully before mutating and applies its writes atomically under a single lock.
- [hard] REQ-6: Template role and anchor names consumed by commands are declared in repository configuration.
- [hard] REQ-7: No two distinct hierarchy-related concepts share a module, type, or CLI-surface name.
- [hard] REQ-8: External-facing docs and the MCP system prompt describe DAG-authoritative containment and the container completion model.

## Notes

Decisions fixed at epic creation: hierarchy resolution canonicalizes on the transitively-reduced graph (rather than exempting containment edges from reduction); template role bindings become configuration with defaults preserving current names.
